extracted.intended_audience: educators, curriculum designers, education students, and policymakers interested in aims and methods of education
extracted.subtask_description: Framework and evaluative criteria for stating and implementing general aims of education (natural development, social efficiency, culture) and for organizing instruction (interest, discipline, subject-matter relevance). Useful for curriculum design and pedagogical evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Social efficiency indicates the importance of industrial competency and the cultivation of capacities so individuals can participate productively in associated life; it is attained not by negative constraint or subordination but by positive use of native individual capacities in occupations having a social meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate into specific aims: enable persons to earn a living, manage economic resources usefully, and avoid being a drag on others; avoid accepting existing economic conditions and standards as final; resist training that fits individuals in advance for definite industrial callings on the basis of parental wealth or status; emphasize adaptability because industries change rapidly; aim to correct unfair privilege and deprivation rather than perpetuate them. Beware of restricting social efficiency to mere external service or output — include sympathetic socialization of mind, ability to share experiences, appreciation of art, and intelligent sympathy (good will).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial competency
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of social efficiency: practical ability to earn one's subsistence and to use products of industry rightly so as not to 'deprave' oneself or injure others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education must not neglect basic vocational and economic competencies; however, training should not be overly specific or rigidly tie pupils to particular callings — it should build adaptable capacities. Avoid selection or placement based on parents' wealth/social status and training that freezes individuals into obsolete methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civic efficiency (good citizenship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifications vaguer than vocational ability; ranges from being an agreeable companion to judging men and measures wisely and participating in making and obeying laws. Emphasizes capacity to share in a give-and-take of experience and to take a determining part in public life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects against purely formal training of mental power; do not interpret narrowly (which would exclude scientific discovery). Include capacities for enjoying and producing art, recreation, and meaningful use of leisure. Cultivate intelligent sympathy and a cultivated imagination for what people have in common; avoid benevolence that dictates rather than frees individuals to find their own good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culture as aim (personal cultivation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Culture means something cultivated and ripened — appreciation of ideas, art, and broad human interests; development of unique, distinctive personal qualities rather than mere average or mediocre refinement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Culture is compatible with social efficiency when attention is given to what is unique in individuals. Avoid conceiving culture as an exclusive, purely 'inner' refinement accessible only to privileged classes. Cultural aim should be socialized — individuals develop in relation to others and communicable experiences. The separation of culture and social efficiency is fatal to democratic education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration and compatibility of general aims
rubrics_metrics.description: General aims (development according to nature, social efficiency, and culture) are points of view for surveying educational problems and must translate readily and consistently into one another's procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test the value of any stated large end by whether it translates into procedures consistent with other aims. Avoid partial or one-sided statements that cause conflict (e.g., treating natural development as spontaneous without nurture, or social efficiency as mere production). Properly understood aims can be reconciled: e.g., social efficiency conceived as capacity to join shared activities entails culture; culture defined as expanding perception of meanings supports efficiency in communal life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest (meanings and role in education)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest denotes (i) a whole state of active development (an occupation/pursuit), (ii) the point at which an object engages or concerns a person, and (iii) the personal attitude of absorption or eagerness toward an object. In education, interest is the connecting force between present powers and intended ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction should discover objects/modes of action connected to pupils' present powers so learning is internally engaged. 'Making material interesting' means revealing genuine connections to pupils' concerns, not adding extraneous pleasurable bribes ('soup-kitchen' pedagogy). Interest is necessary for deliberation, persistence, and intelligent application — without it, reflection and genuine discipline are unlikely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline (will, volition, and persistence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline is the power at command: mastery of resources to carry through chosen actions, involving deliberation, persistence, endurance, and intelligent foresight of consequences; it is positive, not merely subjugation or suffering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate discipline from mere obstinacy (persistence without clear ends) and from shallow intellectual foresight that lacks emotional grip. True discipline requires considered ends and a hold of those ends on the person. Discipline should be cultivated in contexts of interest (connected aims) rather than imposed as blind strain; it develops the capacity to plan, select means, and persist despite distractions and difficulties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter relevance and contextualized study
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter should be studied insofar as it plays a part in carrying forward active lines of interest — things become objects of study when they figure as factors toward ends in which one is engaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize curriculum so facts and skills are presented as conditions for attaining real ends (e.g., numbers as factors in practical activities), not as isolated branches (history, algebra, geography) complete in themselves. Study is effectual when pupils realize the place of the material in activities that concern them; avoid presenting lessons merely to be memorized without perceived connection to pupils' aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejecting the formal-discipline justification without tests
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim that a study 'disciplines' the mind has been used to shield traditional content and methods from criticism; such claims are uncheckable unless linked to specific tests or demonstrable utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demand evidence that a course or method actually produces the asserted disciplinary effects; do not retain subjects merely because they are labeled 'disciplinary.' If a method fails to yield intelligent self-direction, the fault lies with the method, not automatically with the pupil. Replace vague appeals to 'discipline' with concrete considerations of how material engages present powers and promotes reflective, purposive action.
